title: A 2017 GALAH spectrum of TYC 9179-1083-1 shows two stars 42.5 km/s apart; with the timing orbit, the tertiary is brightest and the eclipsing secondary has 0.54-0.70 solar masses, not 0.23
abstract: Campaign studies found a third star on a 5.9-year orbit around the eccentric 10.29-day eclipsing binary TYC 9179-1083-1 from TESS eclipse times (2018-2026), with assumed inner masses of 1.05 and 0.23 solar masses. No study used spectra. We analysed the only available high-resolution spectrum, from GALAH (HERMES, 2017-01-09). Broadening functions in all four arms show a bright component at +29.98 +- 0.15 km/s and a faint component at -12.56 +- 0.34 km/s with about 17 percent of the light. Eleven single-lined stars from the same exposure show no such peak. With the published three-body orbit, only one assignment is possible: the bright star is the tertiary and the faint star is the eclipsed star. The published masses predict a split of 26.4 km/s; the measured split is 42.53 +- 0.77 km/s (21 sigma). Timing refits on 65 fixed inner-mass pairs fit the eclipse times equally well and show that the split needs a secondary of 0.54-0.70 solar masses for any primary of 0.6-1.3 solar masses. A main-sequence light ratio then gives about 0.70-0.88, 0.57-0.62 and 1.05-1.16 solar masses for the three stars. Gaia DR3 RVS statistics reject a dominant eclipsed star and match the median velocity of a dominant tertiary, but the Gaia epoch scatter is smaller than our approximate blend model predicts. The result selects the bright-tertiary branch of the Gaia astrometry. Limits: one spectral epoch, an extrapolated orbit, a possible fourth star that we consider unlikely, and simple light-ratio and blend models. We give velocity forecasts for 2027-2029.

display.caption: Broadening functions of the 2017 GALAH spectrum: a bright component at +29.98 km/s and a faint one at -12.56 km/s in all four HERMES arms (left). Eleven single-lined stars from the same exposure have no second peak (right).

Predicted velocities with the systemic velocity set by the GALAH tertiary. Near the GALAH epoch the published masses put the eclipsed star at +3.6 km/s; the 0.80 + 0.60 solar-mass refit puts it at -12.7 km/s, where the faint component is.
Simulated Gaia DR3 RVS statistics. A dominant eclipsed star is rejected. A dominant tertiary matches the median velocity, but its predicted epoch scatter for m2 = 0.6 is larger than the Gaia value.

citations.reason: We use its three-body timing model, eclipse times, covariance draws and fit code. The GALAH velocity split confirms the predicted sign but excludes its assumed inner masses of 1.05 + 0.23 solar masses.
We reuse its scan-crossing script. The spectrum selects its bright-tertiary Gaia branch and excludes the faint-tertiary branch.
Its high-dilution eclipse-shape fit agrees with the measured dominant tertiary light.
